newsitem.title: ITALY: HPI, Marzotto link-up to create major textile firm.
newsitem.headline: HPI, Marzotto link-up to create major textile firm.

text.p: Italian industrial company HPI, newly formed in a spin-off from financial holding company Gemina, announced over the weekend that it planned to merge with textiles and clothing company Marzotto.
Holding di Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI) and Marzotto, owner of the German menswear label Hugo Boss, said in a statement the new company would be called Gruppo Industriale Marzotto.
"The proposed operation will create one of the largest groups worldwide in the textiles and clothing sector with a significant position in the editorial (publishing) sector," HPI and Marzotto said.
HPI's spin-off from Gemina has meant the transfer to HPI of textile groups Fila and GFT, as well as editorial unit RCS Editori.
Marzotto and HPI said they saw great potential for synergy between operations in the clothing and textiles sectors.

Based on preliminary results for 1996 from the two groups, the new company would have had an estimated revenue of 8.24 trillion lire ($4.85 billion) last year, a net profit of around 253 billion ($149 million) and staff totalling more than 21,000, they said.
